# Phase boundaries

Choose a context transition when it helps the next piece of work. Prefer a meaningful phase boundary, but preserve a continuation record when an interruption occurs mid-phase too.

Before a transition, retain accepted decisions and unresolved work in the existing plan or task record. For ongoing work, use [continuation records](../handoff/CONTINUATION.md). Keep references to primary evidence and the next action; do not rely on an unbroken conversation as the only record.

- Continue when relevant reasoning is still manageable and the next step benefits from it.
- Delegate a concrete independent question or disjoint change when the parent has useful work to do. Give the worker scope, evidence expectations, and an output location. Do not split a shared unresolved decision merely to use another worker.
- Hand off when another session, worker, directory, or tool must resume. Provide the discoverable record and require reconciliation with live state.
- Compact when the next work needs selected context but carrying the whole history would obscure it. Keep the authoritative decisions and evidence in files; the summary points to them.
- Clear only when the current context is irrelevant or the next task can reconstruct what it needs from retained records.

These are task-dependent choices. Fixed token thresholds do not establish reasoning quality. A short summary is useful when the reader can inspect the primary evidence behind a consequential claim. Preserve uncertain conclusions as uncertain through every transition.
